setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Comes early in the set and runs long; the jam is thematic and effective, followed by a powerful outro; Reviewer calls the Bird Song very decent [10][11]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the Oregon show also has a top-three Playin', implying this one is also among the best; Reviewer calls it an extraordinarily cohesive, riveting jam, one of the finest versions of the era [5][11]
- **Promised Land** (1 review): Reviewer dislikes Bob's quasi-falsetto singing and the poor harmonies on this opener [10]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer rates it highly despite a cut in the recording [8]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer considers the stretch from Sugar Magnolia to the end the best part of the show [3]

## The recordings

- **gd72-10-17.sbd.sacks.2219.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 193 min; rated 4.29/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: A cut runs from about 3:30 to 3:54 during a Jerry solo; otherwise sound quality is described as great; Reviewer reports no sound quality problems on this only archive source, which opens with good energy [7][10]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the whole weekend was great; their brother Joe Koetters once had a tape of the show but lost it [2]
- Opening night of a three-night stand; technical problems delayed the start by over an hour, with the crowd getting restless [6]
- Attendee recalls the band playing from after 9pm until about 2am, with probably one long break [6]
- Reviewer says Phil plays with great fire and Bobby throws in tasty licks; some tuning is shaky [8]
- Writer says Jerry called the Fox the best house in the U.S.; rumors had the band considering buying it as a Midwest base [9]
- Reviewer notes several songs are missing from this tape: Jack Straw, Friend of the Devil, Beat It On Down the Line, Ramble On Rose [3]
- Pigpen is noticeably absent, as in all shows from fall 1972 on; band hadn't yet learned to play around that absence, except Oregon [5]
- Reviewer finds the show businesslike with hot jams, but not noticeably better than typical 1972 performances [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-10-17.sbd.sacks.2219.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Mid-source recording (MSR) copied via cassette to DAT, then CDR, extracted with EAC to SHN; from Darrin Sacks, seeded by Jack Warner [1]

## Art and photos

- Poster by gocollect.com: [Grateful Dead Fox Theatre 1972 Value - GoCollect](https://gocollect.com/concert-poster/grateful-dead-fox-theatre-1972) [15]
